reviews.title: Unintuitive and confusing
reviews.text:
Frustrating and confusing to use for underfloor heating

I’m using the Smart Life app to control my electric underfloor heating, and the experience has been unnecessarily complicated.

Setting up something as simple as a heating schedule is confusing. The app presents multiple automation options, temperature settings and conditions without clearly explaining how they work together.

All I want is for my bathroom floor to warm up before I get up in the morning and again in the evening. This should be incredibly straightforward, but instead I’m left wondering whether I’ve configured everything correctly.

The interface isn’t intuitive, the terminology is unclear, and it’s difficult to understand exactly what will trigger the heating to turn on or off.

The app has plenty of functionality, but it really needs a simpler, more user-friendly approach to heating controls, particularly scheduling and temperature management.

Accessibility warning for VoiceOver users regarding Smart Life and Dreamegg

I wanted to share my experience in case it saves someone else some frustration.

I’ve been using products that rely on the Smart Life app for nearly 10 years. Throughout that time, VoiceOver accessibility has been consistently poor. Buttons are often unlabeled, controls can be difficult or impossible to use, and app updates sometimes change the layout or button order, making features that previously worked inaccessible.

Recently I purchased a Dreamegg sunrise alarm clock. I specifically chose it because I was hoping to move away from Smart Life and use a manufacturer’s own app instead.

Unfortunately, dream egg also uses SmartLife! I thought about exchanging the clock for a different model but wanted to try their company app. Dreamegg’s app is also not accessible with VoiceOver.

I contacted both companies.

Smart Life responded that they would pass my feedback along.

Dreamegg responded that their app currently does not support VoiceOver functionality or compatibility with screen readers and that they would share my feedback with their product team.

I’m posting this because many smart home products sold in North America either use the Smart Life platform or their own companion apps, and accessibility information is rarely mentioned before purchase.

If you’re a VoiceOver user, I recommend checking whether a product’s app is actually accessible before buying it, especially if it depends on Smart Li

reviews.title: Buggy app, features behind paywall
reviews.text: I only use this app because I have to for a few of my devices like a couple of smart plugs and a cat food dispenser. Honestly, don’t buy any products that use this app. I work long hours during the day and like to be able to check in and make sure that the cat food dispenser successfully dispensed food. Lately it’s been skipping one of the programmed feedings but for some reason  doesn’t log it in the logs. It’s also in the opposite where the food will dispense, but nothing shows in the log, but if I review the video, it’s there. Extremely inconsistent. Half the time I don’t even get my push notifications and There’s no way for me to set up alerts if the device fails unless I want to pay a ridiculous amount of money per year. I put a memory card in my product to review video because I don’t want to pay their outrageous prices for cloud service as well as paying for a notification feature for device failure separately. Everything today requires a subscription. It’s ridiculous. It feels like a lot of what should be basic features should be included and not be behind a pay wall. In the process of looking for different products that don’t rely on this Chinese app.

reviews.title: Decline in quality
reviews.text:
I’ve used these smart plugs for many years now. At first, I was thrilled with how well everything worked and it was very seamless. Recommended it to a bunch of family and friends, absolutely loved it. 

Recently had to uninstall grandparents’ plugs because it has become wholly unusable for them over the years. Horrible AI features and multiple updates where the response and connectivity of the app noticeably worsened. They said they would rather just get up and turn the light off themselves, which is sad because it used to be extremely helpful for them. 

It was good because it worked and was simple. They lost both of those aspects somehow, it’s like a 50/50 shot at working correctly and/or actually pairing every time I open the app. New features I don’t want and removal of those that were needed. We’ll be switching to another product ourselves if this does not improve drastically soon. Disappointing.
